module.destination: Turn finite evidence models into disciplined posterior updates: respect base rates, derive Bayes, normalize complete hypothesis sets, use odds/LRs correctly, update sequentially without double counting, and stress-test priors/likelihoods.

sessions.title: Conditioning direction: P(E|H) versus P(H|E)
sessions.focus: Distinguish evidence-given-hypothesis from hypothesis-given-evidence.
sessions.purpose: Block the inverse-probability error before Bayes is introduced.
sessions.centralCapability: State the meaning of P(E|H). State the meaning of P(H|E).
sessions.principalObstacle: The same two events appear in both expressions, so learners silently swap the conditioning denominator.

sessions.applicationScope: Finite Bayesian evidence problems with explicit discrete hypotheses, priors and likelihood models.
sessions.transferScope: A changed evidence/hypothesis surface requiring the same update logic and assumption discipline.
sessions.exitCondition: Independently solve and explain M06-S01 on a fresh finite evidence model, including denominators/assumptions.
sessions.lesson: Conditional probability always names the denominator population. P(E|H) asks: among H cases, what fraction show E? P(H|E) asks: among E cases, what fraction are H? Swapping the bar changes the reference set. Worked example: Among100 cases,20 are H; 16 of those show E, while 20 non-H cases also show E. Then P(E|H)=16/20=.8, but P(H|E)=16/(16+20)=4/9. Guided check: In a table with30 H cases,18 H∩E cases and12 non-H E cases, compute both directions.

sessions.lesson: For binary H/H^c, a posterior after E needs the prior P(H) and evidence rates P(E|H), P(E|H^c), or equivalent information giving P(E). If one is missing, many posteriors may fit.
